newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia rebels lay down their arms.
newsitem.headline: Colombia rebels lay down their arms.

text.p: A group of about 110 leftist guerrillas who have vowed to lay down their arms took the first step toward their return to civilian life on Friday in a rural area of northwest Colombia, authorities said.

Army and government officials said the first members of the group surrendered at a pre-arranged time and place on Friday afternoon in the municipality of Tierralta and that all 110 were expected to have demobilized by Saturday.
The rebels are members of the Popular Liberation Army (EPL), which was founded in 1967 and continues to rank as the country's third largest guerrilla group.
A majority of the EPL's 2,000 fighters demobilized in 1991, but a hardcore splinter group continue to operate in the countryside has since grown to about 1,000 fighters.
Fifty members of the EPL demobilized two weeks ago in Cordoba and a regional military official told Reuters the new surrender would make the group virtually non-existent in the country's northwest.
The EPL guerrillas who have surrendered in exchange for amnesty so far operated out of the notoriously violent banana-growing region of Uraba.

The army has conducted a major counterinsurgency campaign in the region in recent weeks. Military sources say the campaign has forced the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) -- the country's largest guerrilla group -- to abandon its strongholds there and stepped up pressure on EPL fighters to surrender.
